mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 or 200 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C180 or C200 petrol typically costs between £500 and £4,500 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M271 units start from £500-£1,500, reconditioned from £1,200-£2,800, and fully rebuilt M274 engines from £2,200-£4,500. A rebuilt M271.DE18 ML engine costs from £2,350, with reconditioned units from £1,800. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 180 or 200 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All C180 and C200 petrol engines use timing chains, not belts. The M271 (W203/W204) uses a single-row timing chain that is considered a wear item - failure typically occurs between 60,000-100,000 miles. The M274 (W205) and M254 (W206) also use timing chains. A rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start is the classic warning sign for timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a C-Class 180 or 200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M271-equipped models (W203/W204, 2000-2013), the most common symptom is a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start. Other signs include the check engine light (P0017 code), rough idle, loss of power, extended cranking, and hard starting. The M271 engine is an interference design - if the timing chain breaks or slips, valves and pistons hit and the engine is effectively junk.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 or 200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W203 or W204 C180/C200 petrol is typically worth £2,500-£8,000 - a rebuilt M271 engine (£2,500-£4,200) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W205 C180/C200 petrol is worth £6,000-£15,000 - a rebuilt M274 engine (£2,200-£4,500) is usually well within the car's value. For the M274, a specialist replacement with an upgraded rebuilt unit is almost always better value than attempting to rebuild the original engine due to the wrist pin design flaw.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M271, M274 and M254 engines in the C180 / C200?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M271 is the original four-cylinder petrol family used in the W203 and W204 (2000-2013), available as supercharged ('Kompressor') and CGI turbocharged variants. The M274 is the turbocharged 1.6L/2.0L engine used in the W205 (2013-2021). The M254 is the 1.5L mild hybrid engine used in the W206 (2021-present) with 48V ISG technology.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 or 200 petrol to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C180 and C200 petrol depends on the engine. On M271 engines, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On M274 engines, the wrist pin/piston seizure failure can cause misfires and power loss. On M254 engines, 48V system faults can cause reduced performance. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 / 200 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C180 and C200 petrol badges have spanned three generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class, evolving from supercharged four-cylinders to advanced turbocharged units with mild hybrid technology. The W203 and early W204 used the M271 engine family - first as supercharged "Kompressor" units, later as CGI turbocharged direct-injection variants. The W205 introduced the M274 turbocharged engine, while the W206 brought the M254 with 48V mild hybrid assistance.

M271.820, 1.8L CGI turbo petrol, 156 hp - W204 C180 CGI launch; direct injection replaces supercharger

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 / 200 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C180 and C200 petrol have been powered by three distinct engine families - the M271 (W203/W204), the M274 (W205) and the M254 (W206). The M271 is notorious for timing chain and camshaft adjuster failure. The M274 suffers from a wrist pin/piston seizure defect that led to an NHTSA investigation. The M254 is newer, with emerging 48V system and oil consumption concerns. problems.group: M271 Timing Chain & Camshaft Adjuster Failure
problems.h4: M271 Timing Chain & Camshaft Adjuster Failure - The Kompressor & CGI Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M271 uses a single-row timing chain that stretches prematurely, often combined with failing camshaft adjusters (phasers). The intake camshaft adjusters break internally, causing a check engine light, extended cranking and a rattle noise on start-up. Symptoms include a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start. P0017 almost always points to a stretched timing chain or a failing camshaft adjuster. The M271 engine is an interference design - if the timing chain breaks or slips, valves and pistons hit and the engine is effectively junk.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, both camshaft adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head removal, valve replacement, piston inspection, full timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has slipped; bent valves almost certain

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt M271 unit with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W204 C180 or C200 petrol is worth £2,500-£8,000. For vehicles under £4,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,100-£1,800) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M271 with warranty (£2,500-£4,200) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts - especially between 60,000 and 100,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£1,100-£1,800) saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Mercedes-Benz extended the warranty on camshaft adjusters for some model years to 10 years/120,000 miles due to the high failure rate - check if your vehicle is still covered.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M271 Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 / 200 petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M274 Wrist Pin / Piston Crack - The 2.0 Litre Petrol Failure
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 and 200 petrol (M274.910 and M274.920, W205, 2013-2021)
problems.rootCause: The M274 engine suffers from a wrist pin / piston seizure failure. The pin that connects the piston to the connecting rod seizes within the piston boss, causing the piston skirt to crack and cylinder bore scoring. Mercedes-Benz published a technical bulletin (LI03-10P060916) regarding a faulty wrist pin that was causing the pistons to eventually crack. The cracked piston can allow engine oil to mix with gasoline, causing white smoke and a burnt smell. An NHTSA investigation was opened into this failure across Mercedes M274-equipped vehicles. The complaint states unfavourable tolerance of the piston wrist pin, resulting in knocking and clattering.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: There is no known preventative repair for the M274 wrist pin fault - it is a design/manufacturing defect that manifests without prior warning signs
Single piston and wrist pin replacement, cylinder hone, new rings, cylinder head gasket replacement, oil system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if compression loss caught immediately

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt M274 unit featuring upgraded pistons designed to address the wrist pin design flaw
repairOptions.longevity: Almost always the better financial decision on a W205

problems.recommendation: The M274 piston crack is the most frustrating failure on this list because there is no preventative fix. The first warning is often a misfire code and rough running. On a 2014-2021 W205 C-Class worth £6,000-£15,000, a specialist replacement with an upgraded rebuilt unit (£2,500-£4,500 fitted) is almost always better value than attempting to rebuild the original engine. Ensure any replacement engine specifically states it has upgraded wrist pin/piston components.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M274 Mercedes-Benz C-Class 180 / 200 petrol engine prices

problems.group: M254 48V Mild Hybrid System & Oil Consumption
problems.h4: M254 48V Mild Hybrid System & Oil Consumption - W206 Emerging Issues
problems.rootCause: The M254 features a 48V integrated starter-generator (ISG) providing up to 15 kW of supplementary electrical output. Early reports indicate oil consumption and 48V battery system issues on some units. The 48V ISG can experience software-related faults.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan, software update, ISG calibration

repairOptions.longevity: Only if engine damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: The M254 is a relatively new engine, and long-term reliability data is still emerging. If you experience warning lights or reduced performance, have the 48V system diagnosed promptly. The ISG and 48V battery are complex components that require specialist handling. The second-generation ISG system can provide up to 15 kW and 200 Nm of additional output.
